# Build execution flow

This describes the current Rust implementation, not a complete correctness or
reproducibility guarantee. The [behavior contract](behavior.qmd) records approved
semantics and the [compatibility log](compatibility.qmd) records evidence and gaps.

## Read-only resolution and preflight

Capture the project root, resolve a private per-run environment without changing
the parent process, require active root configuration,
and merge base/profile/local settings. Validate fields, explicit directory paths,
targets, hooks and destructive destinations. Explicit empty scripts select no
analysis. Otherwise explicit globs or shallow root discovery select inputs;
project rendering may use its own input discovery. Explicit Python-only selection
does not activate an unused Quarto/Bookdown project marker.

Read VERSION with DESCRIPTION/default fallbacks. Check selected interpreters and
configured Git restrictions before controlled project writes. Existing preflight
can still invoke Git/network checks or R package remediation; these are known
limitations, not a clean-environment guarantee.

## Local production build and restoration boundary

Before authoritative writes, capture exact bytes, permissions and presence/absence
for the managed set documented in the compatibility log. This includes VERSION,
ignore/configuration files, existing root regular files, selected in-project
inputs, declared output/docs trees and planned individual rendering artifacts.
External declared output/docs directories are allowed. Linked managed trees are
rejected. Backups stream into private OS temporary storage outside disposable project
cache. Backup creation failure prevents authoritative project writes.

One local error/panic boundary covers ignore synchronization, requested pre-cleanup,
pre/both hooks, script/document execution, renderer configuration, promotion and
post/both hooks. Required output promotion errors propagate. Renderer configuration
is restored exactly, retaining comments and originally absent keys. Candidate
version changes stay in memory; VERSION is written only after those stages succeed.
No pre-build Git commit is created.

On local failure, restore the captured managed set, including originally absent
files/directories. Attempt all restorations; retain recovery backups and report
both the primary and restoration errors when recovery fails. This does not undo
arbitrary script effects outside the captured set or provide a filesystem sandbox,
power-loss atomicity or protection against concurrent filesystem replacement.

## Publication after local success

Storage export and Git publication start after successful local completion. Export
actual declared content before requested `clear_output: post` cleanup. Create one
configured final Git commit, then push when enabled. A publication or later cleanup
failure reports that local analysis succeeded and retains its release/version;
external publication is not rolled back.

Git upstream/authentication policy, stable attempt/release records and an
analysis-free publication retry command remain unfinished. Existing Git push code
still targets origin/main and must not be mistaken for the final policy.

## Development previews and remaining renderer gaps

Previews skip production version changes, cleanup, commits and exports. They run
selected hooks/analysis and restore renderer configuration bytes. Cooperating
scripts must choose appropriate output locations; preview is not automatic output
isolation or an OS sandbox. Individual script subprocesses still start in their
parent directory: the approved root-relative execution and direct R/IDE renderer
parity are separate unfinished work. The existing R package remains untouched.
